web.a_smaller_model_guesses_upcoming_wor: A smaller model guesses upcoming words for the main MLX model to check. Needs a matching helper; up to ~33% faster writing one reply on a split model in our tests, but slower with two chats.
web.reuse_words_from_your_prompt_to: Reuse words from your prompt to help the MLX model write repeated text. Up to ~44% faster in our tests on repeated text, but slower on mixed chats; one chat at a time.
web.reuse_the_beginning_of_repeated_syst: Reuse the beginning of repeated system prompts so the model has less to read. MLX models only.
web.let_two_chats_use_different_minis: Let two chats use different Minis at the same time when an MLX model is split. Up to ~70% more combined output in our tests without a helper; no gain on one Mini, and slower with a helper.
web.how_much_of_the_conversation_the_2: How much of the conversation the model can keep in mind at once. Auto uses the longest context that fits in memory, up to the full context the model was trained for. Native is that full context.
web.combine_small_gpu_steps_when_running: Combine small GPU steps when running an MLX model. Experimental — no meaningful speed gain in our tests; some models are incompatible.
web.store_mlx_chat_memory_more_compactly: Store MLX chat memory more compactly to save RAM; 16 leaves it uncompressed. May lower quality and slow reading; not supported by every model or Native MTP.
web.keep_the_main_gpu_warm_while: Keep the main GPU warm while it waits for another Mini. Split MLX models only; up to ~50% faster writing replies in our tests.
web.a_faster_way_to_read_the_2: A faster way to read the chat so far. Leave on unless a test says off.
web.how_much_of_a_long_question_2: How much of a long question the model reads at once. Larger can read faster and uses more working memory.
web.caravan_learns_from_your_chats_and_2: Caravan learns from your chats and remembers faster settings for each model. Pinned choices stay yours. For GGUF, a change reloads the model when you are not mid-reply.
web.a_smaller_model_of_the_same: A smaller model of the same family guesses upcoming words for the main model to check. It is often faster on code edits and repeated text and helps less on short chats, and the first word on long prompts can come a little later. Gains vary by model and Mac. Auto uses it only when a test on your model finds it faster. On needs a small helper of the same family on this Mac; when Caravan knows one, it offers it under the model and will not download one for you without your OK.
web.reuse_words_from_your_prompt_to_2: Reuse words from your prompt to help with repeated text. Often much faster when the reply repeats the prompt (for example whole-file code edits), little change on short chats, and slightly slower on long prompts. Gains vary by model. Auto stays off until a test finds it is faster.
web.reuse_the_start_of_a_chat: Reuse the start of a chat so later turns begin sooner.
web.let_two_chats_share_the_model: Let two chats share the model at the same time. Auto keeps one chat.
web.store_the_chats_working_memory_more: Store the chat's working memory more compactly. Auto uses the lighter option only when the full one will not fit.
web.native_mtp_uses_the_models_built: Native MTP uses the model's built-in predictor instead of a separate helper. Up to ~46% faster writing replies in our tests; needs a matching MTP head and one chat at a time.

cli.bench.this_measures_prompt_lookup_an:
This measures Prompt lookup and Guess-ahead on {names}.
Each model is loaded once per mode (Off, Prompt lookup, Guess-ahead when a helper is on this Mac, Auto) and runs {v}.
The model that is loaded now is put back at the end, with its settings.

Run: caravan bench {q}--speedups{only}{v_} --yes
cli.bench.no_saved_numbers_for_the_kind: No saved numbers for the {kind} model yet - chat with it a bit, or run the bench.
cli.bench.this_compares_a_gguf_model_to:
This compares a GGUF model to its MLX counterpart and prints
a compact chart of reading, writing, and first-token speed.
It runs {series_txt}. Sizes that were not run are left out.
Pass --details (or --text) to also print the reply-stats
lines. Pass --ascii for plain '#' bars.
cli.bench.when_the_comparison_finishes_o:
When the comparison finishes (or if it stops early), Caravan puts
the original model back, if one was loaded.

On the 1st Mac, with Caravan running and both models already
downloaded:

  caravan bench --gguf {gid} --mlx {mid}{flags} --yes
cli.bench.to_only_print_already_saved_ch:
To only print already-saved chat averages, without loading anything:

  caravan bench --gguf {gid} --mlx {mid} --from-averages

Caravan's page is http://127.0.0.1:{port}/
cli.bench.the_model_did_not_become_ready: The model did not become ready in time.
cli.bench.or_using_the_name_caravan_benc:

install.usage_text:
Usage: bash scripts/install.sh [--role lead|worker] [--repo PATH] [--ref REF]
       [--python PATH] [--check] [--dry-run] [--no-start] [--update] [--use-existing]
Worker plan: --model PATH [--counts K,K,... --stage-index I --listen HOST:PORT]
             [--upstream HOST:PORT | --peer HOST:PORT] [--name ID] [--port PORT]
Each Mac gets its browser page; a fixed-model worker is a developer option.
